name: goth-corpus
policy: Cultural and aesthetic material only. No sexualized content of anyone; mature aesthetics are documented strictly as fashion history and academic commentary, applied only to adult-coded contexts. Nothing here is erotic content.

history.event: Gothic rock emerges from UK post-punk: Siouxsie and the Banshees, Bauhaus, Joy Division, The Cure.
Leeds F Club and London's Batcave (opened 21 July 1982, 69 Dean Street, Soho) become the subculture's cradles; NME briefly calls the scene 'positive punk' before settling on 'goth' in 1983.
Batcave peak: house band Specimen, Alien Sex Fiend, cabaret nights, horror films; DIY fashion culture defines the look. Compilation 'Young Limbs and Numb Hymns' (1983).
Second wave diversifies: darkwave, ethereal wave (Cocteau Twins' Elizabeth Fraser, Dead Can Dance's Lisa Gerrard), steampunk and Victorian goth offshoots.
Global spread via club culture and the internet; cybergoth hybridizes with rave/industrial; US deathrock revival seeds.
Mall goth era via Hot Topic; Gothic Lolita crosses from Japan through manga/anime; scholarly study begins (Hodkinson's 'Goth: Identity, Style and Subculture', 2002).
Tumblr-born pastel goth; Afrogoth community challenges colorism; goth becomes a durable global aesthetic umbrella.

fashion_guide.makeup: Pallor base, cool-toned contour, extended inner-eye line joining brow to nose bridge (trad), sharp painted lips or deep oxbloods; modern looks range from graphic white liner (cyber) to candy tones (pastel).
fashion_guide.staples: Black layered clothing, fishnets, corsetry, lace, velvet, leather; silver jewelry, ankh/bat/cross motifs, chokers; boots from winklepickers to platforms.
fashion_guide.diy_ethos: Batcave origin story: clothes were hand-painted, customized, repurposed - women's tights as sleeves, vintage suits, found jewelry. Authenticity never depended on budget.
fashion_guide.historical_roots: Elizabethan and Victorian mourning wear, Gothic literature (Poe, Stoker, Shelley), horror cinema (Hammer films, Universal monsters), symbolist art.

mature_aesthetics_academic.disclaimer: Summaries of peer-reviewed cultural-studies literature. Fashion history and sociology only - not erotic material.

four_pillars.victoriana: Victorian mourning dress and corsetry embody fear of death plus nostalgia for the past (Journal of Fashion Business analysis of 1980s goth style).
four_pillars.vampirism: Vampire costume and diabolical imagery as decadence performance, drawn from B-movies, Christian/Egyptian/Celtic mythologies.
four_pillars.androgyny: Gender-blurring silhouettes across all genders - a defining subcultural value since the Batcave.
four_pillars.fetish_fashion_history: Corsetry, latex, leather and bondage-derived hardware adopted as aggressive self-expression and theatrical style. Weinstock's 'Gothic Fetishism' (Duke UP, Goth: Undead Subculture) reads it as aesthetic/horror-inflected display rather than invitation. Siouxsie Sioux's BDSM-influenced stagecouture is analyzed academically as 'alternative femininity' - emancipatory visibility within a male-dominated industry.

gender_studies: Wilkins, 'So Full of Myself as a Chick': Goth Women, Sexual Independence, and Gender Egalitarianism (Gender & Society) - goth women used scene-celebrated boldness to resist passive-femininity norms.
Schilt, 'Queens of the Damned' - women's participation across two gothic subcultures.
Manchester Gothic Studies (2018) - 21st-century goth magazines often market hyperfeminine neo-traditional beauty ideals.
Hodkinson (2002) - goth noted among subcultures with notably strong female participation and media self-production.
literature_excerpts_topics: Edgar Allan Poe - decadence and mourning aesthetics
Bram Stoker's Dracula - vampiric seduction of the modern imagination
Anne Rice and Poppy Z. Brite - gothic fiction beloved by the scene

glossary.Batcave: London club-night (1982-86) considered goth's birthplace; attendees called Batcavers.
glossary.Ethergoth: Retroactive name for mid-80s romantic/feminine goth style (Siouxsie, Fraser, Gerrard influence).
glossary.Deathrock: US parallel strand of goth with heavier punk residue.
glossary.Darkwave: Goth-adjacent genre fusing goth rock with synthpop/new wave.
glossary.Winklepickers: Sharp-pointed vintage boots/shoes, trad goth staple.
glossary.Perky goth: Self-aware term for goths with sunny temperaments ('goth is about the music and the drama, not misery').

facts_nightly_pool: The Batcave entrance featured a real coffin you walked through.
NME coined then dropped 'positive punk' before John Peel announced the term 'goth' on BBC radio, June 14 1983.
Siouxsie Sioux rejected the 'Godmother of Goth' title - she considered the Banshees too witty for 'the doom, the black'.
Alexander McQueen's MA collection 'Jack the Ripper Stalks His Victims' lined jackets with human hair - haute couture's debt to goth.
Anny, NAVER's open parametric human body model, is built on MakeHuman community assets - the same open-source spirit the Batcave DIY ethos championed.
Robert Smith, Nick Cave and Siouxsie were all Batcave regulars watching house band Specimen.
Pastel goth was born on Tumblr around 2010 - the first goth style the internet created rather than the club.
The 1983 Batcave compilation 'Young Limb and Numb Hymns' carried UK goth to North America.
